Stainless-steel hex locknut, M42 x 1.5, falls under heading 7318 (screws, bolts, nuts...). Nuts of iron or steel are classified in 7318.16. Stainless steel nuts go under 7318.16.30 (stainless steel nuts) in the 2022+ schedule? Checking the structure:

7318.16 Nuts:
- 7318.16.10 Self-locking nuts
- 7318.16.20 Other, of stainless steel? Actually: 7318.16.30 "Other: Of stainless steel" with 7318.16.3000? Older schedule: 7318.16.10 self-locking nuts (7318.16.1000?), 7318.16.30 Other: Of stainless steel... In the HTSUS: 7318.16.10 "Self-locking nuts" (subdivided: 7318.16.1000?). I recall 7318.16.30 "Other: Of stainless steel", 7318.16.50 "Other: Hex nuts, not of stainless... ", 7318.16.60 "Other", 7318.16.90.

The HTS actually has: 7318.16.10 Self-locking nuts: 7318.16.1030 ... Then 7318.16.20 "Other: Of stainless steel" 7318.16.2000? Hmm. I believe: 7318.16.30.00 "Other nuts: Of stainless steel"? I recall 7318.16.5000 "Other: Of iron or steel with a hex..." I'll go with self-locking nuts: 7318.16.1000 doesn't ring... Self-locking nuts are 7318.16.10.00 I think; the "locknut" here is described as resisting loosening, so self-locking.

{"hts_code": "7318.16.1000", "reason": "A hex locknut designed to resist loosening under vibration is a self-locking threaded nut of iron or steel (stainless) under heading 7318, subheading 7318.16 for nuts."}
